metadata.note: Great Northern Railway's Chicago-Seattle flagship passenger trains, the historical predecessors of Amtrak's Empire Builder (which kept the name). Geometry east of Minneapolis and west of Moorhead is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment (see amtrak.geojson). The Minneapolis-Moorhead portion is NOT: Amtrak rerouted the Empire Builder off the Great Northern main line and onto the ex-Northern Pacific line through St. Cloud, Staples, Wadena and Detroit Lakes on Oct 1 1979, when the North Coast Hiawatha was discontinued, dropping the Willmar, Morris and Breckenridge stops. That portion was re-traced from OpenStreetMap on 2026-08-27 onto the real Great Northern route via Willmar and Breckenridge; see each feature's geometry_quality. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones (train introductions, renamings, mergers, discontinuation dates); headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Empire Builder, Oriental Limited, Western Star, Willmar station, Breckenridge station), gnrhs.org, american-rails.com; OpenStreetMap for the Minneapolis-Moorhead geometry
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: No Great Northern employee or public timetable has been checked for this feature. Open questions: (1) whether the Oriental Limited used the Willmar line for its whole 1909-1947 run or was routed via the St. Cloud - Sauk Centre - Fergus Falls - Barnesville line at any point -- the St. Cloud line is not drawn anywhere in data/; (2) whether either train used the 1912 Surrey Cutoff (New Rockford - Surrey) rather than the Grand Forks - Devils Lake main line this feature draws; (3) all headway_min values.
metadata.geometry_audit: 2026-08-27: Minneapolis-Moorhead re-traced from the ex-Northern Pacific Staples Subdivision onto the ex-Great Northern Wayzata/Morris/Moorhead Subdivisions. Detected by sampling the traced line against town coordinates (Sauk Centre 51 km off, Fergus Falls 52 km, Breckenridge 67 km, Willmar 86 km) and confirming the corridor's OSM name. Sources: Wikipedia 'Willmar station' (station was on the Great Northern main line, Northern Transcon) and Wikipedia 'Breckenridge station' (Empire Builder moved to the former Northern Pacific corridor after the North Coast Hiawatha ended in 1979).

properties.geometry_quality: Re-traced 2026-08-27. Minneapolis-Moorhead (250.0 mi) is now real-traced from OpenStreetMap along the BNSF Wayzata, Morris and Moorhead Subdivisions -- the ex-Great Northern main line via Wayzata, Delano, Litchfield, Willmar, Benson, Morris, Herman and Breckenridge -- replacing the previous alignment, which wrongly followed the ex-Northern Pacific BNSF Staples Subdivision via St. Cloud, Staples, Wadena and Detroit Lakes. Amtrak did not move the Empire Builder onto that Northern Pacific corridor until Oct 1 1979, eight years after this feature's drawn era ends, so the old geometry was a later alignment than the era (CLAUDE.md Rule 2). Traced 250.0 mi Minneapolis-Moorhead against a raw OSM path of 402.3 km; simplified Douglas-Peucker at 25 m, both splice joins under 15 m, no straight-line bridging. West of Moorhead and east of Minneapolis the geometry is unchanged and still comes from the modern Amtrak GTFS alignment, which for those stretches is the same physical ex-GN line -- except that this feature draws the Portland section as its west end and does not show the Seattle main, and it has not been checked against the Surrey Cutoff (New Rockford-Surrey, 1912) in North Dakota. Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 30 ruled segments totalling 466 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).
